text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm proposing we converge on a single prefetch strategy for safetensors + mixed-format bundles. TL;DR: prefer index-first warmup when an index exists, fall back to streamed chunk warmup for unknown blobs. Thoughts?

raj: +1 to index-first for predictable latency, but worried about tail OOMs when large layers get pulled eagerly.

linh: can we make the warmup policy pluggable per model? e.g., "policy: index-first" or "policy: streaming-prefetch" in the model manifest. Keeps runtime simple.

maria: yes, pluggable makes sense. we need clear defaults though — most customers should get index-first.

owen: agree defaults to index-first, but we should add a cheap probe to detect very large shard headers and switch to streamed fallback automatically. probes should be constant-time (read header size + estimated tensor byte sum).

raj: what about bundles that mix safetensors + legacy .pt shards? The loader needs a format abstraction to hide these differences.

linh: propose a small FormatAdapter trait: load_header(), stream_chunk(), mmap_fallback(). Minimal surface area. Implementation per format handles partial-read semantics and chunk alignment.

maria: pseudo-config I'm thinking:
```
model_manifest:
  name: foo-v2
  bundles:
    - uri: s3://...
      format: safetensors
      warmup_policy: auto
    - uri: s3://...
      format: pytorch-legacy
      warmup_policy: streaming
```
Behavior: auto => index-first if index present and shard <= threshold, else streaming.

owen: we'll need eviction signals from the cache manager to the warmup coordinator. If warmup is inflight and eviction triggers, warmup should be cancellable and resume-able.

raj: +1. Also ensure warmup jobs don't block critical inference threads; they should run at low QoS with backpressure tokens.

linh: Suggest warmup state machine states: pending -> probing -> streaming/indexing -> paused (evicted) -> completed -> verified. expose metrics: warmup_latency, bytes_streamed, probe_time, cancellations.

maria: good call. We should also have a verification pass that checks checksums after hot-swap, but skip for local dev mode.

ci-bot: note saved: https://ci/reports/warmup-policy-experiments/6612345678 

owen: ops question — how do we signal that streaming fallback was used? We want telemetry to route future requests away from nodes hitting streaming often.

linh: emit a tag on the model-load span: "warmup.path=streaming" or "warmup.path=index-first". Metrics aggregator can create a per-node score.

raj: performance tradeoff: streaming reduces peak memory but increases first-token latency; index-first can spike memory but gives lower p95. Need a knob to tune per-customer SLO.

maria: action items:
- linh: draft FormatAdapter interface & a reference safetensors + legacy adapter (due EOD Wed)
- owen: implement probe heuristic + cancellable warmup job (due Fri)
- raj: telemetry keys + metric dashboards to distinguish paths (due next Tue)
- maria: write short RFC addendum clarifying default policy and threshold numbers (due Mon)

maria: one last nit — add compatibility test cases for mixed-format bundles and simulate eviction mid-warmup in CI.

ci-bot: added job: warmup-eviction-sim in matrix (runs on PRs).

raj: also add a tiny benchmark that measures p50/p95 first-token latency for both paths under a small sample of models.

maria: agreed. keeping it conservative: default threshold 512MB per shard for index-first, tuned later with metrics.

linh: I'll include a fallback manifest field `fallback_order: [index-first, streaming]` so we can experiment with ordering without changing code.

owen: thanks — sounds actionable. If no objections I'll merge the addendum tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

maria: none from me. go ahead. :rocket:

raj: no objections.

sre-bot: FYI: created incident-tune-warmup SLO task under infra board.

maria: closing thread — will link RFC addendum here once drafted.
